decisions.reason: Bounded embeddings do not bound an arbitrary input map. In dimension two choose p_i=(1/i,0), token vectors encoding bits, and f_in(v,p)=(1/p_1,v_1) on these inputs. Linear query/key/value projections select position, bit, and bit respectively. With EOS bit zero, a single nonfinal one has EOS attention weight exp(n)/(exp(n)+n-1), tending to one; the all-zero word gives zero. A Lipschitz update can return this weighted bit. Added a uniform bound on the actual combined initial states for the soft-influence regime; this excludes the counterexample without restricting the general hard model.

The rejection treats F3 as an arbitrary existential lookup, but proof 3.3 uses its explicit construction. In lem-yun-transformer-grid-lookup, proof 1.2 takes key and value projection u, proof 2.1 preserves the delta lattice and uses half-grid thresholds, and proofs 6.1 and 7.1 place detector and pulse boundaries delta/3 from valid lattice codes. Every maximizing tie has the same scalar value u^T Z. The final query is nonzero except on the all-zero grid state: positive nonconstant codes are shifted above zero, negative sentinel codes stay negative, and an unshifted constant zero code means every column is zero. At that state all values vanish, so its softmax output is stable under perturbation as well. Fixed continuous ramps and finite composition therefore justify the simulation. No repair is needed.
